title: Press behind a fret
summary: Use a small, comfortable press for a clear sound.

steps.title: Press behind a fret
steps.body:
**fretboard** means the playing surface along the neck where you press strings

**Why it matters:** Its picture is the map we use for playing.

**fret** means a thin metal bar crossing the fretboard

**Why it matters:** It marks a place that changes the vibrating string length.

Press string 6 just behind the first metal bar, on the headstock side. Keep your fingertip near the bar, not on top of it. Pluck gently. If it buzzes, move a little closer and use only enough pressure to make it clear. Keep your thumb relaxed behind the neck and your wrist comfortable. Stop if it hurts.

steps.title: Look and listen
steps.body: Fret 0 in the picture means open. Fret 1 is the space just before the first metal bar. The lit places show open string 6 and its first fret; listen to the change.

items.prompt: Play the lit note. Tap it here, or play one string with the microphone.

steps.title: Take your time
steps.body: Alternate open string 6 and the first fret slowly. Clear sound matters more than speed. The screen can guide the place but cannot check your posture or buzzing.

items.prompt: Where do you press to play the first fret clearly?
choices: just behind the first metal bar
on top of the metal bar
items.answer: just behind the first metal bar
